intro.paragraph: I'm Javier Alberto Baró Morales. I build the frontend of web products — interfaces, component systems, and the interaction layer people actually use. Earlier roles were full-stack; the work I take now is Angular first, with React and Next.js when the product requires them, and getting the UI right in production.

work.note: How I take on demanding frontend work — from the constraint to a production interface.

method.statement: Interface first, then the system that keeps it honest.

freelance.description: Product UI, component systems, and frontend architecture for web applications.

getecsa.description: Shipped web application work across the stack; strongest ownership on the interface.

rootstack.description: Web solutions and application UI for client products.

stack.statement: Angular is the framework I know deepest. TypeScript, React, Next.js, HTML, and CSS sit with it. Accessibility and performance are part of the build, not a pass at the end.

system.statement: Angular is the framework I know deepest. TypeScript, React, Next.js, HTML, and CSS sit with it. Accessibility and performance as part of the build, not a pass at the end.

education.paragraph: Computer systems engineering, then years shipping software. The focus now is frontend.

workflow.note: How I take on demanding frontend work — from the constraint to a production interface.

scope.title: Scope the problem
scope.body: Challenge work starts with the constraint: the broken flow, the missing states, the interface that already failed.

specify.title: Specify the interface
specify.body: Empty, error, and success paths first. Layout and type are decided before a component is named.

build.title: Build the system
build.body: Angular is the primary stack. React and Next.js when the product is built that way. Components are the contract.

ship.title: Ship it readable
ship.body: Accessible, performant, and typed — left so the next engineer can follow the intent.

interface.title: Interface first
interface.body: Start from what the person sees and does. Layout, type, and state before the rest of the stack.

components.title: Components as the contract
components.body: Reuse is a system, not a folder of similar files. Tokens, variants, and clear ownership.

ship.title: Ship it honest
ship.body: Accessible, fast enough, and typed. Performance and a11y are part of the build, not a later pass.

readable.title: Leave it readable
readable.body: The next engineer should see the intent. Structure over cleverness.
